## What it is

Solid Ø36 column on the tower axis, Z 18.7 to 47.0. Its flat bottom stands on the adapter's flat top, placed by a `scale_dowel` pressed into it; it carries the cup grille's seat in a top socket. Weak magnets (two Ø5 x 2) in wells open at the bottom face, strong magnets (two Ø8 x 3) in the top socket's floor. Printed upright as modelled, bottom on the bed. Bambu PETG Basic.

## Design notes

- Modelled in the machine frame and ends with `scale_frame`.
- Lower joint: flat on flat. Well depth = magnet height + `weak_magnet_gap` - adapter magnet recess (0.2) = 3.3 at the default gap of 1.5 (1.0 felt far too strong on the first print); the magnet is pushed to the well's end. The parameter defaults to the layout value; raise it to weaken the joint (two pairs on purpose: one pair would need a second dowel against rotation). Under each lower magnet, a Ø2.5 push-out hole (`push_out_hole`) runs up to the upper socket's floor (22 mm): a pin about 25 mm long, pushed down from the socket, gets the magnet out, so a trial gap does not cost magnets.
- Dowel hole: Ø4.8 (`dowel.tower_hole`, 0.10 under the dowel), 4 mm deep, over the adapter's key hole at (92, 54). A dowel pushed home stands 1 mm proud. One dowel 5 mm off the axis sets the position; the magnet pairs turn the tower into line. The dowel's short, coned engagement lets the tower tip off the weak magnets when the grille is lifted.
- The upper socket is `scale_seat` with the seat height plus the socket clearance (0.5), so its flanks coincide with the grille's boss and its floor stays 0.5 clear.
- Upper joint: wells in the socket floor going down, depth = magnet height + `strong_magnet_gap` - socket clearance (0.5) = 4.0 at the default gap of 1.5, the magnet pushed to the well's end; the grille's are flush in its boss. Under each, a Ø2.5 push-out hole from the bottom face (21 mm); under the west one (92, 54) it runs through the dowel's bore, which is why the dowel is hollow.
- Three `hole_ceiling` warnings, accepted: where a push-out hole starts over a lower well's end (two) and over the dowel hole (one).
- Printed upright: the lower wells and the dowel hole open on the bed, their ends are 5 mm bridges. The bottom socket's 20 mm bridge, pierced by the wells, sagged on the first print; it is gone.
- Plastic: the upper wells are 15 mm clear of the lower ones.
- Lightening is not wanted: solid body, infill makes it light.
- Polish: 1 mm on the outer top rim only. Nothing on the bed face or the sockets.

## Don't

- Do not put a bottom socket back: its ceiling was a 20 mm bridge broken by the well mouths, and it sagged (2026-11-17).
- Do not lengthen the dowel's reach into the adapter: past about 1 mm the tower can only come off straight up the dowel's axis.
- Do not chamfer the socket edges or flanks, nor the bottom face: they mate.
- Do not hollow it out.
- Do not edit the well depth by hand: change `weak_magnet_gap`.
- Do not drop to one pair of lower magnets: the joint is weakened by `weak_magnet_gap`, and one pair would let the tower turn about the dowel (2026-11-17).
- Do not remove the final `scale_frame`: without it the part prints as its mirror image (found 2026-11-16: the PCB box came out on the wrong side of the cell).

- 2026-11-17 - Ø1 push-out hole on each lower magnet's axis, from the upper socket's floor, so trial gaps reuse magnets. The lower joint felt very strong at 1.0: tune it with `weak_magnet_gap`.
- 2026-11-17 - Both joints 1.5 apart (`weak_magnet_gap` 1.0 -> 1.5, new `strong_magnet_gap` 0.5 -> 1.5); push-out holes Ø1.5 under all four magnets.
